one_month_reasoning: No Jabil earnings fall in the window to 2026-11-01: Q4 FY26 was reported 2026-09-30 and Q1 FY27 results are expected mid/late December. Events in the window: (1) the FY26 Form 10-K, likely filed in late October, with full-year segment income, customer concentration and working-capital footnotes. This matters because inventory rose to $7.4B and accounts payable to $14.4B, but it is rarely a price mover. (2) Late-October hyperscaler earnings and capex guidance (Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Meta). This is the biggest swing factor for AI-infrastructure EMS names in either direction. (3) The late-October FOMC. The stock fell about 10% on a beat-and-raise (low about $284), then recovered to $304 by 10-02. Guidance came in about 6% above consensus EPS ($17.55 vs $16.58), and a director bought shares near $300 in July. Both lean slightly toward positive drift after the overreaction, but the effect is small and uncertain. So I stay near a symmetric lognormal around $304 at the usual monthly vol (47%/3.5, about 13.4%), with a slight upward tilt (P(>=304.41) = 0.52).

fair_value.method: Blend of 16x my FY28 (Aug-2028) core EPS of $20.75 = $332 (60%) and a 5.5% FCF yield on FY28E adjusted FCF of about $19/share = $345 (40%). In Oct 2027 the market will price the stock on FY28 numbers.

bear.story: AI/data-center capex digestion in 2027, or loss or insourcing at a hyperscaler (the top 5 customers are about 36% of revenue). FY27 misses its back-end-loaded margin ramp, the FY28 outlook in Sept 2027 is flat at about $17 EPS, the working-capital unwind hurts FCF, and the multiple de-rates to about 11.5x (below the 5-year average).

base.story: FY27 lands at or slightly above the $17.55 guide. The second hyperscaler becomes a 10%+ customer and the third ramps. The Sept 2027 FY28 outlook implies about 15% EPS growth to about $20.75, valued at about 16x.

bull.story: A repeat of the FY26 beat-and-raise pattern (+19% vs the initial guide): FY27 about $19.5, and the FY28 outlook is about $23-24 with core margin of 6.5%+. AI revenue tracks well above $22.1B, the market re-rates toward the summer-2026 multiple at about 20x, and buybacks continue.

thesis_break_reason: About 12x the FY27 guide and about 30% below today. A trade there would most likely mean the market has evidence that the $44.5B / $17.55 outlook is breaking: a guide cut at the Dec or Mar quarter, a hyperscaler program loss, or AI capex retrenchment. It would also put the stock below the 52-week low area that preceded the AI re-rating. Ordinary volatility (about 47%) produced swings from $284 to $377 over the past three months without going below about $285.

reasoning: Primary documents anchor the view. The Q4 FY26 8-K shows revenue of $36.0B (+21%), core EPS of $13.09, and adjusted FCF of $1.53B. FY27 guidance is $44.5B revenue, 6.1% core margin, $17.55 core EPS and about $1.6B FCF. That is well above both the June call's framing (about 15% growth) and consensus ($16.58), yet the stock fell about 10% to a $284 low before closing at $304.41. At that price JBL trades at 17.3x guided FY27 EPS and about 14.7x my FY28E. The FY26 track record (initial guide of $11.00 vs actual $13.09) suggests the guide is conservative. The balance sheet tempers that: receivables, inventory and prepaid rose by about $7.6B, mostly funded by about $8B of payables and accruals, and FCF barely grows despite +24% revenue. That supports the market's skepticism about quality and cyclicality. Insider data is mixed but small: officers sold small amounts in July at $316-345, and a director bought 500 shares at $299.63 on 2026-07-17. Valuation: 16x FY28E $20.75 = $332 and a 5.5% FCF yield = $345, blended to $337, about 11% above spot. Scenarios: bear $195 (25%), base $335 (50%), bull $480 (25%), mean about $336. For the ladder I used a lognormal-like distribution with median about $325 and sigma about 0.43, slightly below the 47% realized vol because the guide gives near-term earnings visibility. The left tail is kept fat for an AI-capex air pocket, which is the dominant risk for an EMS name with about 50% AI exposure. The late-Sept 2027 FY28 outlook lands days before the horizon date, so outcome dispersion stays high. Research was limited because the Q4 FY26 slide deck and the company-hosted transcript were not yet posted (404). Segment and AI figures come from a third-party transcript recap.
